comparator.name: Maastricht Science Programme (BSc)
comparator.sourceNotes: Maastricht’s 180 EC degree combines a 30 EC core, 10 EC of general education, 110 EC of electives and a 30 EC thesis. Students build their own profile through courses, skills training and research projects. The example keeps elective choices open within the programme’s level and catalogue rules.

components.name: Introduction to Biology
components.note: Core course in biological processes, from molecules and cells to organisms.

components.name: Introduction to Chemistry
components.note: Core course in chemical structure, bonding, reactions and equilibria.

components.name: Introduction to Physics
components.note: Core course in physical principles and mathematical problem-solving.

components.name: Introduction to Liberal Arts and Sciences
components.note: Core course in philosophy of science, research ethics, argumentation and science communication.

components.name: Introduction to Scientific Research I
components.note: Core skills training in laboratory safety, experimental design, measurement and lab reporting.

components.name: Introduction to Scientific Research II
components.note: Core skills training that builds on the first laboratory course through experimental design, data analysis and reporting.

components.name: Introduction to Project Period
components.note: Core project that integrates the first two teaching periods through a collaborative literature review and poster presentation.

components.name: General education: mathematics
components.note: Choose one 5 EC mathematics course from the approved list.

components.name: General education: humanities or social science
components.note: Choose one 5 EC humanities or social-science course from the approved list.

components.name: Elective courses in a chosen science profile
components.note: Choose fourteen courses for a science profile. In the standard 5 EC pattern, at least four are advanced and at most three introductory.

components.name: Elective skills training
components.note: Choose eight skills modules. At least two are advanced and at most two introductory.

components.name: Elective research projects
components.note: Choose four projects. At least one is advanced and at most one introductory.

components.name: Bachelor Thesis Research
components.note: Complete the 30 EC research thesis in the final semester. Entry requires 145 EC, with limited coursework and a project allowed to be awaiting grades.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option combines experimental life science with Earth systems, ecology and quantitative analysis. Neuroscience has its own brain, cognition and biomedical sequence. The third option adds sustained modeling and imaging methods to biological foundations. Pairwise differences are 1/2: 13 courses each way, 1/3: 11 courses each way, 2/3: 7 courses each way. Sustainability Essentials I and Environmental Biogeochemistry substantively address applied physical and chemical principles, but available courses do not build the general chemistry, physics and materials depth needed for a separate direction. UCR offers laboratory and analytical preparation for independent work, and optional independent research outside the plans.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce the biology of living systems. UCR emphasizes molecules, cells and human biology.
Maastricht introduces general chemistry. UCR Biochemistry covers chemical processes in living organisms.
Maastricht requires introductory physics. UCR applies selected physical principles in sustainability and Earth science courses.
Both develop experimental skills. UCR’s laboratory course emphasizes biochemical and molecular methods.
Both develop experimental design and data analysis. Maastricht applies them in a dedicated laboratory skills course.
Maastricht integrates the core courses through a collaborative literature review and poster presentation.
Maastricht teaches philosophy and communication of science in a dedicated course.
Maastricht requires one mathematics choice. UCR develops mathematics across several scheduled courses.
Maastricht requires one approved humanities or social-science course.
Maastricht students choose courses for their own science profile. The three UCR plans illustrate distinct combinations.
Maastricht students choose eight additional skills modules. UCR teaches related methods within its scheduled courses.
Maastricht students complete four additional research projects in dedicated project periods.
Maastricht requires a 30 EC thesis. UCR independent research is optional and sits outside the scheduled degree.

notes.text: Maastricht requires dedicated introductory chemistry and physics and offers specialist electives in both. The UCR plans draw on related principles in biochemistry, Earth science and sustainability. They also develop biology, laboratory work and quantitative methods.

Maastricht combines a fixed science core with a self-designed profile, recurring skills modules and research projects, and a 30 EC thesis. UCR develops related methods within scheduled courses and offers optional independent research separately.
